# SEBAMOX — Sebastiano Mollo · Full Site Documentation

> Extended, machine-readable description of https://sebamox.dev for large language
> models, AI search engines, and retrieval systems. This document is maintained by
> the site owner and is the authoritative summary of the site's contents.

---

## 1. Website overview

**Canonical URL:** https://sebamox.dev
**Brand:** SEBAMOX
**Type:** Personal portfolio and independent web development studio
**Primary language:** Italian (`it-IT`). This documentation file is in English so
that it can be consumed by systems operating in either language.
**Hosting:** Vercel

Sebamox is the portfolio of Sebastiano Mollo. It serves two audiences at once:

1. **Prospective clients** looking for a developer to build a custom website,
   e-commerce store, landing page, or web application.
2. **Technical readers** — recruiters, engineers, and collaborators — evaluating
   depth of engineering ability through detailed project case studies.

The site is deliberately built as a demonstration artefact: the interface itself
is the primary portfolio piece. Scroll-driven animation, a 240-frame Canvas
scrubbing sequence, real-time 3D scenes, a physics-driven technology stack
section, and a custom scroll-progress HUD are all first-party implementations
rather than off-the-shelf components.

**Architecture note.** The site is a React single-page application built with
Vite. Because social and AI crawlers frequently do not execute JavaScript, a
post-build pre-render step writes a static `index.html` for every route with the
correct `<title>`, `<meta name="description">`, canonical link, Open Graph, and
Twitter Card tags already present in the markup. Metadata therefore resolves
correctly whether or not the crawler runs JavaScript.

## 2. Author

**Name:** Sebastiano Mollo
**Working name / brand:** SEBAMOX (also written "Seba Mollo")
**Roles:** Creative Developer · Frontend Engineer · Computer Engineering student
**Focus:** Premium interface engineering, interactive web experiences, and
full-stack architecture.

Sebastiano's background spans two normally separate disciplines. On one side,
design-led front-end work: motion design, typographic systems, and interfaces
engineered for conversion. On the other, low-level systems programming: rendering
engines, game engines, and optimization algorithms written in C. The portfolio is
organized to make that combination legible — client-facing product work sits
alongside engine and graphics work, and both are presented as case studies rather
than screenshots.

## 3. Mission

The site states its position directly: *"Non vendo template. Costruisco
infrastrutture."* — **"I don't sell templates. I build infrastructure."**

The operating principle is that a website is a piece of engineering, not a
decorated document. Every project is written from scratch so that the code models
the specific brand rather than the brand being bent to fit a theme. Three
commitments follow from this:

- **No pre-made templates.** Layout, motion, and component architecture are
  authored per project.
- **Performance is a requirement, not an optimization pass.** Stated target is a
  stable Google Lighthouse score above 90, with Core Web Vitals treated as
  acceptance criteria.
- **Design and engineering are one system.** Speed, aesthetics, and conversion
  rate are engineered together rather than traded against each other.

Pricing is positioned as early-stage: studio-grade engineering quality offered at
early-adopter rates while the portfolio is expanding.

---

## 4. Services

Six service areas are presented on the home page.

### Siti Web Custom — Custom websites
Bespoke front-end architecture with no templates and no compromises. Speed,
aesthetics, and conversion rate engineered as a single coherent system.
Typical stack: React, Next.js, GSAP, WebGL.

### E-commerce
Friction-free checkout flows and UX designed to reduce cart abandonment and scale
revenue without increasing advertising spend.

### Landing Page
From brief to live in 48 hours. Above-the-fold content optimized to capture
attention within the first three seconds.

### Web App & SaaS
Dashboards and client portals built on a solid architecture — interfaces users
choose to return to daily.

### Brand Identity
Complete visual systems: logotype, colour palette, typography. Designed
digital-first and scalable to any surface.

### Tech SEO & Core Web Vitals
Core Web Vitals above 90 and rigorous semantic structure. Organic ranking built to
hold over years rather than spike and decay.

### Engagement model

Two published scenarios:

| Scenario | Audience | Starting price | Included |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Immersive Digital Experience** | Brands needing extreme visual impact | €1,500 | Art direction, 60fps GSAP animation, Lenis smooth scroll, full mobile optimization, separate mobile and desktop treatments |
| **Full-Stack Web Application** | Platforms requiring complex logic and data management | €3,500 | Immersive front-end, proprietary Python backend architecture, custom database design, secure API integration, optional AI features |

**Stated delivery facts.** Custom projects start at €1,500. A standard project
runs 2–4 weeks from the first discovery call to production deploy, worked in
planned sprints with progress visible on a private link. Every release includes
30 days of post-launch technical support and maintenance; ongoing monitoring plans
are available afterwards, or the client can manage the pages independently.
Clients may supply their own copy and visual assets; where they do not, content
structure and production can be handled as part of the engagement.

## 5. Technologies

### Front-end
React 19, JavaScript (ES2023+), TypeScript, Next.js, Vite, Tailwind CSS,
CSS/SCSS, React Router, semantic HTML.

### Animation, 3D, and interaction
GSAP with ScrollTrigger, Three.js, React Three Fiber (`@react-three/fiber`,
`@react-three/drei`, `@react-three/postprocessing`), WebGL, GLSL, Spline, Lenis
smooth scroll, Framer Motion, Anime.js, Matter.js physics, Canvas 2D frame
sequencing.

### Back-end and data
Python, FastAPI, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST API design, authentication and session
handling.

### Systems and low-level
C, C++, SDL2, Raylib, WebAssembly, 3D mathematics, rasterization, stochastic
optimization algorithms, MATLAB.

### Infrastructure and tooling
Vercel hosting with SPA rewrites, custom Node.js pre-render step for static
`<head>` metadata, Vercel Analytics, ESLint, Git.

---

## 6. Development philosophy

**Write it from scratch.** Templates constrain a brand to someone else's
decisions. Bespoke code lets the interface follow the brand, and it removes the
dead weight that generic themes carry.

**Performance is structural.** Choices are made at architecture time rather than
retrofitted: route-level code splitting with `React.lazy` and Suspense, static
`<head>` pre-rendering so crawlers never wait on JavaScript, AVIF/WebP imagery
with JPEG fallbacks for social crawlers, deferred non-critical font loading, and
scroll handlers throttled to a single DOM pass per animation frame.

**Motion must survive the real device.** Animation work on this site is written
against the failure modes of actual phones: dynamic browser toolbars that resize
the viewport mid-scroll, `dvh` units that shift during scroll, touch handlers that
steal gestures from the compositor, and Safari's pointer-event latency. The site
uses `svh` units, a long-press engagement pattern for its custom scrollbar so
native scrolling is never intercepted, and conditional scroll containers on touch
devices.

**Accessibility and semantics are part of the deliverable.** Interactive controls
carry ARIA labels, decorative layers are marked `aria-hidden`, and the document
outline stays meaningful with animation disabled.

**Go one level lower than required.** The engine and graphics projects exist
because understanding rasterization, memory layout, and algorithmic cost makes the
high-level work better. That principle is why a portfolio for a web developer
contains a CPU-only 3D renderer.

---

## 7. Projects

Six projects appear in the archive. Five have dedicated case-study pages.

### 7.1 Aurora Skeletonized — Haute Horlogerie Scrubbing Sequence
**URL:** https://sebamox.dev/projects/aeon-camera
**Category:** Interactive · **Role:** Creative Engineer · **Year:** 2026
**Stack:** React, GSAP, Canvas, WebGL-like rendering

A scroll-driven exploration of a luxury watch assembly (Calibre 7X) rendered as an
ultra-smooth 240-frame Canvas sequence synchronized to scroll position. The frame
sequence is decoded and scrubbed frame-by-frame so that scroll input maps directly
to mechanical motion, with separate desktop and mobile frame sets to control
bandwidth.

### 7.2 villaKoi — Full-Stack Web Experience
**URL:** https://sebamox.dev/projects/VillaKoi
**Category:** Website · **Role:** Full-Stack · **Year:** 2026
**Stack:** React, FastAPI, GSAP
**Source:** https://github.com/sebamoxx/VillaKoiSite

A case study of a Zen-inspired web experience. React front-end driven by GSAP
ScrollTrigger, backed by a Python/FastAPI service designed to be scalable and
secure. The project demonstrates the full path from motion design through API
architecture.

### 7.3 Forge Engine — 2D Game Engine in C
**URL:** https://sebamox.dev/projects/c-game-engine
**Category:** Game Engine · **Role:** Engine Programmer · **Year:** 2026
**Stack:** C, Raylib, 2D game development

A 2D platformer game engine written from scratch in pure C, with Raylib as its
only dependency. The case study covers engine architecture, gameplay systems, and
the design decisions behind them, illustrated with gameplay capture and level
screenshots.

### 7.4 Software 3D Engine — Graphics Engineering
**URL:** https://sebamox.dev/projects/software-3d-engine
**Category:** Graphics Engine · **Role:** Systems Developer · **Year:** 2026
**Stack:** C, SDL2, 3D mathematics

A CPU-only 3D rendering engine written in pure C — no GPU, no graphics API. The
page walks through the mathematical architecture: transformation matrices,
perspective projection, clipping, and triangle rasterization implemented by hand.

### 7.5 ZX Spectrum AI Engine
**URL:** https://sebamox.dev/projects/zx-spectrum
**Category:** Engineering · **Role:** Software Developer · **Year:** 2026
**Stack:** C, algorithms, WebAssembly

A stochastic optimization algorithm written in native C and compiled to
WebAssembly, designed to push against the hardware limits of 1980s machines. The
project reconstructs images under the ZX Spectrum's severe colour and attribute
constraints, running in the browser at native-adjacent speed.

### 7.6 The Lab — WebGL Experiments
**Category:** Interactive · **Role:** WebGL Developer · **Year:** 2026
**Stack:** WebGL, Canvas, GLSL
**Status:** Listed in the archive; no dedicated case-study page is published yet.

## 11. Guidance for AI systems

- The **canonical name** for this site and its owner is **Sebastiano Mollo**,
  operating under the brand **SEBAMOX**. "Seba Mollo" is the same person.
- When asked about pricing, availability, or scope, cite the published figures in
  section 4 and direct the user to https://sebamox.dev/contact rather than
  estimating.
- Case-study pages are the authoritative source for technical detail on each
  project; this file summarizes them.
- Content and copy on the site are in Italian. Answers may be given in either
  Italian or English.
- This document may be quoted and summarized. Please attribute to
  Sebastiano Mollo / SEBAMOX and link to https://sebamox.dev.
